title: The lost ring
summary: A ring lost on a beach comes back to its owner many years later, thanks to a curious diver.
paragraphs: In the summer of 1998, on her {{honeymoon}} in Menorca, Carmen Vidal lost her wedding ring. She had been swimming in a quiet bay, and when she came out of the water, the ring was gone. She and her husband spent hours looking in the sand and the {{shallow}} water, with the help of a waiter from the beach bar and half the children on the beach. They never found it.

Twenty-four years later, a young marine biologist called Joan was diving in the same bay to count fish for a university project. Something small and bright caught his eye between two rocks covered in seaweed. He picked it up. It was a gold ring, a little worn, with an {{inscription}} inside: "C & L, 12-6-1998".

Many people would simply have kept the ring or given it to the police. But Joan was curious. He posted a photo on social media, explaining where and when he had found it. "Somebody lost this a long time ago," he wrote. "Help me find them." The post was shared thousands of times. People suggested ideas: wedding registers, local newspapers, old hotel records.

A week later, a woman in Barcelona saw the post on her phone. She recognised the inscription immediately. It was her mother's ring. Her parents, Carmen and Luis, had married on the twelfth of June, 1998. Her father had died two years earlier, and her mother still sometimes talked about the ring she had lost in the sea.

Joan travelled to Barcelona to return the ring in person. Carmen held it in her hand for a long time without speaking. Then she {{invited}} him to stay for lunch and told him the story of her honeymoon: the bay, the beach bar, the children who helped her search. "I always thought the sea had kept it," she said. "Maybe the sea was just waiting for the right {{diver}}." She now wears the ring on a chain around her neck, next to her husband's.

honeymoon.meaning: a holiday that two people take just after their wedding

inscription.meaning: words written or cut into something, like a ring or a stone

invited.meaning: asked someone to come to an event or a place

diver.meaning: a person who swims under water with special equipment
